newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares lower, lack impetus to move higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares lower, lack impetus to move higher.

text.p: German share dealers bemoaned the lack of serious widescale buying interest in German equities on Wednesday, and said while individual stocks were doing well, overall sentiment was muted.
At 1354 GMT the IBIS DAX index was down 5.44 points at 2,558.15 points, having traded in a fairly narrow range over course of the day, moving between 2,555.70 and 2,574.60 points.
One Frankfurt trader said: "With little interest rate speculation to feed on, people are feeding on fundamentals. This is great for individual stocks but it's not good for moving the overall market."
"We need some new impulse to bring us across the record threshold. If we do break the all-time high (2,589.91 points), it will only be for a couple of days," the trader said.

The Dow Jones index opened higher and Bunds dropped earlier gains but stayed steady in afternoon trade. However, the possible boosting effects of these factors on German shares were outweighed by the continued weakness of the dollar.
"New York helped a little, but the dollar is dragging and doesn't look like getting much stronger," a trader said.
The highest volume of trade was in Daimler Benz AG, which reports half-year figures on Thursday.
Daimler was up one mark at 81.20 marks in afternoon trade. German chemical stocks had another good day, boosted by an influx of foreign investors eager to increase their weighting in the sector.
In later trade there was some evidence of profit-taking in the chemical sector. Hoechst AG was up three pfennigs at 52.60 marks, off earlier highs
BASF AG was lower, down 30 pfennigs at 44.09 marks, having gone ahead in earlier trade, and Bayer AG was also off earlier highs, down 60 pfennigs at 53.50 marks.
Volkswagen was higher in afternoon trade.
The carmaker was up 8.60 marks at 549.50 marks after it said its first half deliveries were up 13.5 percent at 1.451 million cars.
